Section 3 • Transmitted Flux

3.7 Product of Total Overfluxes

Now, let’s compute the product of two total overfluxes at different coordinates \((\vec{x}_{\perp\alpha},\, \Lambda_\alpha)\) and \((\vec{x}_{\perp\beta},\, \Lambda_\beta)\); a term \(\mathcal{S}_p\mathcal{S}_q\) is of order \(n=p+q\), so we collect the terms with the same \(n\): \begin{align} \delta^{(s)}(\vec{x}_{\perp\alpha},\,\Lambda_\alpha)\, & \delta^{(s)}(\vec{x}_{\perp\beta},\,\Lambda_\beta) = \frac{1}{1+\mathcal{C}(\Lambda_\alpha)} \frac{1}{1+\mathcal{C}(\Lambda_\beta)} \notag \\ & \Bigg[ \underbrace{ \sum_{n=0}^{L} \sum_{p=0}^{n} \mathcal{S}_p^{(s)}(\vec{x}_{\perp\alpha},\,\Lambda_\alpha)\, \mathcal{S}_{n-p}^{(s)}(\vec{x}_{\perp\beta},\,\Lambda_\beta) }_{\textrm{orders } 0\,\le\, n\,\le\, L} + \underbrace{ \sum_{n=L+1}^{2L} \sum_{p=n-L}^{L} \mathcal{S}_p^{(s)}(\vec{x}_{\perp\alpha},\,\Lambda_\alpha)\, \mathcal{S}_{n-p}^{(s)}(\vec{x}_{\perp\beta},\,\Lambda_\beta) }_{\textrm{orders } L+1\,\le\, n\,\le\, 2L} \Bigg]. \tag{3.33} \end{align}

Within each order we separate the terms containing \(\mathcal{S}_0^{(s)}\) from those containing only overfluxes. For \(n=0\) the only term is \(\mathcal{S}_0^{(s)}(\Lambda_\alpha)\,\mathcal{S}_0^{(s)}(\Lambda_\beta)=\mathcal{C}(\Lambda_\alpha)\,\mathcal{C}(\Lambda_\beta)\). For \(n=1\) we have that: \begin{align} \sum_{p=0}^{1} -\mathcal{S}_p^{(s)}(\vec{x}_{\perp\alpha},\,\Lambda_\alpha)\, -\mathcal{S}_{n-p}^{(s)}(\vec{x}_{\perp\beta},\,\Lambda_\beta) = \mathcal{C}(\Lambda_\alpha)\,\mathcal{S}_{1}^{(s)}(\vec{x}_{\perp\beta},\,\Lambda_\beta) + \mathcal{S}_1^{(s)}(\vec{x}_{\perp\alpha},\,\Lambda_\alpha)\,\mathcal{C}(\Lambda_\beta) \qquad 1\le n\le L, \notag \end{align}

For \(2\le n\le L\): \begin{align} \sum_{p=0}^{n} \mathcal{S}_p^{(s)}(\vec{x}_{\perp\alpha},\,\Lambda_\alpha)\, \mathcal{S}_{n-p}^{(s)}(\vec{x}_{\perp\beta},\,\Lambda_\beta) &= - \mathcal{C}(\Lambda_\alpha)\,\mathcal{S}_{n}^{(s)}(\vec{x}_{\perp\beta},\,\Lambda_\beta) - \mathcal{S}_n^{(s)}(\vec{x}_{\perp\alpha},\,\Lambda_\alpha)\,\mathcal{C}(\Lambda_\beta) +\dots \notag \\ &\quad \dots + \sum_{p=1}^{n-1} \mathcal{S}_p^{(s)}(\vec{x}_{\perp\alpha},\,\Lambda_\alpha)\, \mathcal{S}_{n-p}^{(s)}(\vec{x}_{\perp\beta},\,\Lambda_\beta) \notag, \qquad 2\le n\le L, \notag \end{align} The orders above \(L\) contain only products of overfluxes, and no \(\mathcal{S}_0^{(s)}\) appears in them.

Therefore, substituting back these decomposed terms in (3.33) we obtain: \begin{align} \delta^{(s)}(\vec{x}_{\perp\alpha},\,\Lambda_\alpha)\, & \delta^{(s)}(\vec{x}_{\perp\beta},\,\Lambda_\beta) = \frac{1}{1+\mathcal{C}(\Lambda_\alpha)} \frac{1}{1+\mathcal{C}(\Lambda_\beta)} \notag \\ & \Bigg[ \underbrace{ \mathcal{C}(\Lambda_\alpha)\,\mathcal{C}(\Lambda_\beta) }_{\mathrm{order}\, 0} \underbrace{ - \mathcal{C}(\Lambda_\alpha)\,\mathcal{S}_{1}^{(s)}(\vec{x}_{\perp\beta},\,\Lambda_\beta) - \mathcal{S}_1^{(s)}(\vec{x}_{\perp\alpha},\,\Lambda_\alpha)\,\mathcal{C}(\Lambda_\beta) }_{\mathrm{order}\, 1} + \notag \\ & \underbrace{ \sum_{n=2}^{L} \left( - \mathcal{C}(\Lambda_\alpha)\,\mathcal{S}_{n}^{(s)}(\vec{x}_{\perp\beta},\,\Lambda_\beta) - \mathcal{S}_n^{(s)}(\vec{x}_{\perp\alpha},\,\Lambda_\alpha)\,\mathcal{C}(\Lambda_\beta) + \sum_{p=1}^{n-1} \mathcal{S}_p^{(s)}(\vec{x}_{\perp\alpha},\,\Lambda_\alpha)\, \mathcal{S}_{n-p}^{(s)}(\vec{x}_{\perp\beta},\,\Lambda_\beta) \right) }_{\mathrm{orders}\, 2 \leq n \leq L} + \notag \\ & + \underbrace{ \sum_{n=L+1}^{2L} \sum_{p=n-L}^{L} \mathcal{S}_p^{(s)}(\vec{x}_{\perp\alpha},\,\Lambda_\alpha)\, \mathcal{S}_{n-p}^{(s)}(\vec{x}_{\perp\beta},\,\Lambda_\beta) }_{\textrm{orders } L+1\,\le\, n\,\le\, 2L} \Bigg]. \tag{3.34} \end{align}

3.7.1 Subset-Pair Representation of the Product

To make the combinatorial structure of the product in Eq. (3.34) more transparent, it is useful to organize the different contributions in tabular form. Each column represents one subset-term selected from the \(\Lambda_\alpha\)-dependent bracket, and each row represents one subset-term selected from the \(\Lambda_\beta\)-dependent bracket. In this way, each cell directly identifies one contribution to the full product. More explicitly, an entry written as \(A/B\) means that the subset-term \(A\) is taken from the \(\Lambda_\alpha\) bracket and the subset-term \(B\) is taken from the \(\Lambda_\beta\) bracket. For example, in the case \(L=3\), the entry \(23/123\) denotes \[ \delta_{2}^{(s)}(\vec{x}_\perp,\Lambda_\alpha)\, \delta_{3}^{(s)}(\vec{x}_\perp,\Lambda_\alpha)\, \delta_{1}^{(s)}(\vec{x}_\perp,\Lambda_\beta)\, \delta_{2}^{(s)}(\vec{x}_\perp,\Lambda_\beta)\, \delta_{3}^{(s)}(\vec{x}_\perp,\Lambda_\beta). \] The symbol \(\mathcal{C}\) refers to the zeroth-order \(\mathcal{C}(\Lambda)\) contribution, which actually enters the product as \(-\mathcal{C}(\Lambda)\) – note the minus sign. The cell colors indicate the total order of each contribution, namely \(|A|+|B|\), so that all terms with the same total order share the same color.

Just to illustrate the combinatorial structure of the product, we explicitly write the full expansion for the case \(L=2\). For compactness, let us define \begin{align} \delta_{j}^{(s)}\!\left(\vec{x}_\perp,\Lambda_\alpha\right) &\coloneqq \delta_j^{(s)}(\vec{x}_\perp,\Lambda_\alpha), \qquad \delta_{j,\beta}^{(s)} \coloneqq \delta_j^{(s)}(\vec{x}_\perp,\Lambda_\beta). \tag{3.35} \end{align} Then, for the case \(L=2\), we obtain: \begin{align} &\delta^{(s)}(\Lambda_\alpha)\,\delta^{(s)}(\Lambda_\beta) = \frac{ 1 }{ \bigl[1+\TextZero{\mathcal{C}(\Lambda_\alpha)}\bigr] \bigl[1+\TextZero{\mathcal{C}(\Lambda_\beta)}\bigr] } \Bigg[ \notag\\[0.3em] &\qquad\quad \underbrace{ \TextZero{\mathcal{C}(\Lambda_\alpha)\,\mathcal{C}(\Lambda_\beta)} }_{\textcolor{black!70}{\text{order }0}} - \underbrace{ \TextOne{\mathcal{C}(\Lambda_\beta)\,\delta_{1,\alpha}^{(s)}} - \TextOne{\mathcal{C}(\Lambda_\beta)\,\delta_{2,\alpha}^{(s)}} - \TextOne{\mathcal{C}(\Lambda_\alpha)\,\delta_{1,\beta}^{(s)}} - \TextOne{\mathcal{C}(\Lambda_\alpha)\,\delta_{2,\beta}^{(s)}} }_{\textcolor{cyan!22!black}{\text{order }1}} + \notag\\[0.6em] &\qquad + \underbrace{ \TextTwo{\delta_{1,\alpha}^{(s)}\delta_{1,\beta}^{(s)}} + \TextTwo{\delta_{2,\alpha}^{(s)}\delta_{2,\beta}^{(s)}} + \TextTwo{\delta_{1,\alpha}^{(s)}\delta_{2,\beta}^{(s)}} + \TextTwo{\delta_{2,\alpha}^{(s)}\delta_{1,\beta}^{(s)}} }_{\textcolor{green!22!black}{\text{order }2}} \notag\\[0.6em] &\qquad \underbrace{ - \TextTwo{\mathcal{C}(\Lambda_\beta)\,\delta_{1,\alpha}^{(s)}\delta_{2,\alpha}^{(s)}} - \TextTwo{\mathcal{C}(\Lambda_\alpha)\,\delta_{1,\beta}^{(s)}\delta_{2,\beta}^{(s)}} }_{\textcolor{green!22!black}{\text{order }2}} + \notag\\[0.6em] &\qquad + \underbrace{ \TextThree{\delta_{1,\alpha}^{(s)}\delta_{1,\beta}^{(s)}\delta_{2,\beta}^{(s)}} + \TextThree{\delta_{1,\alpha}^{(s)}\delta_{2,\alpha}^{(s)}\delta_{1,\beta}^{(s)}} + \TextThree{\delta_{2,\alpha}^{(s)}\delta_{1,\beta}^{(s)}\delta_{2,\beta}^{(s)}} + \TextThree{\delta_{1,\alpha}^{(s)}\delta_{2,\alpha}^{(s)}\delta_{2,\beta}^{(s)}} }_{\textcolor{yellow!22!black}{\text{order }3}} + \underbrace{ \TextFour{\delta_{1,\alpha}^{(s)}\delta_{2,\alpha}^{(s)}\delta_{1,\beta}^{(s)}\delta_{2,\beta}^{(s)}} }_{\textcolor{orange!22!black}{\text{order }4}} \Bigg]. \tag{3.36} \end{align}

For illustrative purposes, we also present the table corresponding to the case \(L=3\). The same color scheme is used to indicate the total order of each contribution.
